sections.title: People to know
sections.intro_md:
You have met Guru Ghasidas, Vir Narayan Singh, Teejan Bai and Habib Tanvir. A few more names complete the picture.

**Ajit Jogi** (1946 to 2020) was an IPS and IAS officer turned politician who became the state's first Chief Minister in 2000. His claim to Scheduled Tribe status was challenged for years, and a state committee rejected it in 2019.

**Raman Singh**, an Ayurvedic doctor, ran the state for 15 years (2003 to 2018); his cheap-rice scheme made the public distribution system a model for others.

**Vishnu Deo Sai**, of the Kanwar tribe from Jashpur, became Chief Minister in December 2023.

**Shankar Guha Niyogi** organised the iron-ore miners of Dalli-Rajhara and built a workers' hospital and schools; he was murdered in Bhilai in 1991.

**Pt. Sundarlal Sharma** led anti-untouchability work and the 1920 Kandel canal satyagraha in Dhamtari, and is remembered as the dreamer of a separate Chhattisgarh.

**R. H. Richharia**, the rice scientist, spent his last decades collecting Chhattisgarh's rice varieties.

sections.title: Recap
sections.intro_md:
Chhattisgarh in one breath: a landlocked state of 1 November 2000, ninth by area, carved from Madhya Pradesh, one-third Adivasi and more than 40 per cent forest. Its plains are the rice bowl of India, with a gene bank of some 20,000 rice varieties in Raipur. Its ground holds a fifth of India's coal output, rich Bailadila iron and all its tin, feeding Bhilai's rails and Korba's power.

Its past runs from a rock theatre at Ramgarh to the brick Laxman temple at Sirpur, the animal-bodied god of Tala, Kalachuri Ratanpur and the carved walls of Bhoramdeo. Its reformers fought caste with a white flag (Satnam) and with ink (the Ramnamis). Its arts are Pandavani, Panthi, Raut Nacha and the bison-horn dance; its foods chila, bore basi, chapda and mahua.

Bastar keeps a 75-day Dussehra with no Ravana, and in 2026 the state declared the end of a 40-year insurgency there. Remember three pictures: a stolen chariot, a face covered in the name of Ram, and a woman swinging a tambura like Bhima's mace.

cards.front: Name this festival and the town it is held in.
cards.back: Bastar Dussehra, Jagdalpur: the hand-pulled chariot of the goddess Danteshwari.

cards.front: How long does Bastar Dussehra last, and is Ravana burnt?
cards.back: About 75 days, from Hariyali Amavasya to after Vijayadashami. No Ravana is burnt; it honours Danteshwari and village gods.

cards.front: Why do villagers 'steal' the Bastar Dussehra chariot?
cards.back: In the Bahar Raini rite, men from nearby villages take the chariot at night to Kumhdakot; the king must go there, offer new rice to the goddess and bring it back.

cards.front: Which waterfall is this, and on which river?
cards.back: Chitrakote Falls on the Indravati, about 38 km west of Jagdalpur: India's widest waterfall.

cards.front: How wide and how high is Chitrakote in full flood?
cards.back: Close to 300 m wide; about 29 to 30 m high.

cards.front: What makes this tattooed man's community distinctive?
cards.back: He is a Ramnami: members tattoo the name Ram on their bodies, a protest begun in the 1890s against being barred from temples.

cards.front: The Ramnamis won a court case over their right to use Ram's name in ____.
Who founded the Satnami movement, and what is its symbol?
cards.back: Guru Ghasidas (born 1756, Giroudpuri). The jaitkham: a white pole with a white flag.

cards.front: What is this tall white tower and where is it?
cards.back: The jaitkham at Giroudpuri Dham, birthplace of Guru Ghasidas; about 77 m, taller than the Qutub Minar.

cards.front: Who is this singer and what art does she perform?
cards.back: Teejan Bai, Pandavani: the Mahabharata sung and acted with a tambura.

cards.front: What did Teejan Bai do at 13 that broke a rule of Pandavani?
cards.back: She sang standing, in the Kapalik style, when women were expected to sit (or not sing at all).

cards.front: Kapalik or Vedamati: which school improvises from memory?
cards.back: Kapalik improvises (Teejan Bai). Vedamati follows a written verse text (Jhaduram Dewangan).

cards.front: In Pandavani, what does the tambura become?
cards.back: Bhima's mace, Arjuna's bow, a chariot, Draupadi's hair: it is the only prop.

cards.front: Name the dance and the people who perform it.
cards.back: The gaur dance of the Bison-horn Maria of southern Bastar.

cards.front: Name this cowherds' dance.
cards.back: Raut Nacha, danced by the Raut (Yadav) after Diwali, from Dev Uthani Ekadashi.

cards.front: What are these women dancing around?
cards.back: A clay parrot in a basket: Sua nacha, the women's clapping dance of the Diwali season.

cards.front: Which Habib Tanvir play, acted by Chhattisgarhi folk actors, won at Edinburgh in 1982?
cards.back: Charandas Chor, the thief who never lies.

cards.front: Panthi is the dance of which community, in praise of whom?
cards.back: The Satnamis, in praise of Guru Ghasidas. It ends in human pyramids.

cards.front: Which temple is this, and what is it built of?
cards.back: Laxman Temple, Sirpur, around 595 to 605 CE: one of India's finest brick temples.

cards.front: Which Chinese pilgrim visited Sirpur, and when?
cards.back: Xuanzang, in 639 CE. He reported about 100 monasteries.

cards.front: What is strange about this statue from Tala?
cards.back: Its face and body are made of animals and extra faces; a 5th to 6th century Rudra-Shiva, about 7 ft and 5 tonnes.

cards.front: Which temple is called the Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh?
cards.back: Bhoramdeo, near Kawardha, completed around 1089.

cards.front: What might the Sitabenga cave on Ramgarh hill be?
cards.back: One of India's oldest theatres (3rd century BCE), with rock-cut benches for an audience.

cards.front: Which dynasty ruled the Chhattisgarh plains from Ratanpur for centuries?
cards.back: The Kalachuris (Haihayas), from about 1000 CE to the Maratha conquest in the 1740s.

cards.front: Which goddess's temple is this, and what does the town's name mean?
cards.back: Danteshwari, Dantewada: 'danta' is tooth; a tooth of Sati is said to have fallen here.

cards.front: When was Chhattisgarh formed and who was its first Chief Minister?
cards.back: 1 November 2000, from Madhya Pradesh. Ajit Jogi.

cards.front: What share of Chhattisgarh's people were Scheduled Tribes in 2011?
cards.back: 30.6 per cent (7.8 million).

cards.front: What does Chhattisgarh's name mean, and why is that doubted?
cards.back: Thirty-six forts. No one has listed all 36; some prefer Chedisgarh, after the Chedi (Kalachuri) kings.

cards.front: Who was Vir Narayan Singh?
cards.back: Zamindar of Sonakhan who gave a merchant's grain to famine victims in 1856, rebelled in 1857, and was hanged in Raipur on 10 December 1857.

cards.front: What was the Bhumkal of 1910 and who led it?
cards.back: An Adivasi uprising in Bastar against forest laws and officials, led by Gunda Dhur, who was never caught.

cards.front: What craft is this, and how are the thread-like lines made?
cards.back: Bastar dhokra: lost-wax brass casting. The lines were threads of beeswax wound on the clay core.

cards.front: What is kosa?
cards.back: Chhattisgarh's tussar silk, from wild silkworms on forest trees; woven around Champa and Janjgir. Honey-gold and textured.

cards.front: What is this dish?
cards.back: Chila: a rice-flour pancake, Chhattisgarh's everyday breakfast.

cards.front: These ants become which Bastar dish?
cards.back: Chapda: red-ant chutney, crushed with chilli and salt; sour from formic acid.

cards.front: What is collected from this tree before dawn in spring, and what is it made into?
cards.back: Mahua flowers: eaten, sold, and distilled into mahua spirit.

cards.front: What is bore basi, and which day celebrates it?
cards.back: Rice soaked overnight in water, eaten cold. Bore Basi Tihar is 1 May, Labour Day.

cards.front: About how many rice varieties are in the Raipur gene bank, and who collected most?
cards.back: About 20,000 accessions; R. H. Richharia led the collection in the 1970s.

cards.front: What is the state animal, and why is it a worry?
cards.back: The wild water buffalo. Only a few dozen survive in central India; females are almost absent.

cards.front: Name the state bird.
cards.back: The common hill myna: black, orange beak, yellow wattles, and a famous mimic.

cards.front: Which plateau, called the Shimla of Chhattisgarh, has a Tibetan settlement?
cards.back: Mainpat, Surguja, settled by Tibetans in 1962 to 1963.

cards.front: What is this mine and why is it famous?
cards.back: Gevra, Korba: about 59 million tonnes of coal in 2023 to 24, ranked the world's second-largest coal mine.

cards.front: What is the only mineral Chhattisgarh produces alone in India?
cards.back: Tin concentrate.

cards.front: What does Bhilai Steel Plant supply that nobody else in India does?
cards.back: 260-metre rails, the longest made in India.

cards.front: What is Hasdeo Arand?
cards.back: About 170,000 ha of forest in north Chhattisgarh, the largest unfragmented forest in central India, over about 5 billion tonnes of coal; a long fight over mining.

cards.front: What does Abujhmarh mean, and what happened there in May 2025?
cards.back: The unknowable hills. CPI (Maoist) chief Basavaraju was killed in an encounter there.

cards.front: What was Salwa Judum, and what did the Supreme Court rule in 2011?
cards.back: A state-backed anti-Maoist militia (from 2005). The court ordered the state to stop arming civilians as special police officers.

cards.front: When and where was India declared Naxal-free?
cards.back: 20 May 2026, by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, at Jagdalpur.

cards.front: What youth institution is this?
cards.back: A ghotul, the Muria youth house where unmarried chelik and motiari learn songs, work and rules.

cards.front: Whose tattoos are these, and what is the tradition called?
cards.back: Baiga women's godna: tattoos added at set ages, said to be the only ornament taken to death.

cards.front: What are Chhattisgarh's two official languages, and what is Halbi?
cards.back: Hindi and Chhattisgarhi. Halbi is Bastar's link language between tribes.

cards.front: What happens at Hareli?
cards.back: First festival of the farm year (Shravan new moon): tools worshipped, neem twigs on doors, children walk on gedi stilts.

cards.front: Where is Rajim and why is it holy?
cards.back: South-east of Raipur, where the Mahanadi meets the Pairi and Sondur: Chhattisgarh's Prayag, with the Rajiv Lochan temple.

cards.front: Teejan Bai's highest civilian award, and when did she die?
cards.back: Padma Vibhushan (2019). She died on 5 July 2026 at AIIMS Raipur.

cards.front: What is sulfi?
cards.back: The fermented sap of the fishtail palm Caryota urens: Bastar's milky palm drink.

cards.front: What is the resource curse? (side dish)
cards.back: The pattern, first named by economist Richard Auty in 1993, in which places rich in minerals or oil often grow more slowly, govern worse and fight more than places without them.

cards.front: Name two ways a resource curse works. (side dish)
cards.back: Dutch disease (a booming resource crowds out farming and industry) and rent-seeking (whoever controls the resource can rule without needing the people's taxes or consent).

cards.front: Whom did the Bastar kings claim descent from?
cards.back: The Kakatiyas of Warangal, through Annam Dev, traditionally in 1324. Historians call the link tenuous.

quiz.prompt: Match each dance to its people.
quiz.explanation: Each dance belongs to a community and season.

quiz.prompt: Match the food to what it is.
quiz.explanation: The basics of the Chhattisgarhi plate.

quiz.prompt: Is Chhattisgarh's area (135,192 km²) higher or lower than England's (about 130,000 km²)?
quiz.explanation: Slightly larger than England.

quiz.prompt: Gevra produced about 59 million tonnes of coal in 2023 to 24. Is its planned capacity higher or lower than that?
quiz.explanation: It is being expanded to 70 million tonnes a year.

quiz.prompt: Which of these was NOT a caste-reform movement born or rooted in Chhattisgarh?
quiz.explanation: Satnami (Guru Ghasidas), Ramnami Samaj and the Damakheda Kabir Panth seat are all here; the Lingayat movement began in Karnataka.

quiz.prompt: Which is NOT a GI-tagged product of Chhattisgarh?
quiz.explanation: Bastar Dhokra, Jeeraphool and Nagri Dubraj are Chhattisgarh GIs; Similipal red-ant chutney is Odisha's.

quiz.prompt: Guess the person.
quiz.explanation: The Pardhi singer who made Pandavani famous worldwide.
clues: She sang standing when women were told to sit.
Habib Tanvir took her to Delhi.

quiz.prompt: Guess the place.
quiz.explanation: Bhoramdeo temple near Kawardha.
clues: A Shiva temple at the foot of the Maikal hills.

quiz.prompt: Chhattisgarh's name is popularly said to mean
quiz.explanation: Thirty-six forts, though no list of 36 exists.

quiz.prompt: In 2022 the Chhattisgarh assembly unanimously resolved against new mining in Hasdeo Arand.
quiz.explanation: July 2022, an all-party resolution; felling for an existing mine later resumed.

quiz_bank.prompt: How many states does Chhattisgarh border?
quiz_bank.explanation: Seven: Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.

quiz_bank.prompt: Chhattisgarh was carved out of Odisha in 2000.
quiz_bank.explanation: It was carved out of Madhya Pradesh, on 1 November 2000.

quiz_bank.prompt: Chitrakote Falls is famous above all for its
quiz_bank.explanation: Width: close to 300 m in flood, the widest in India. It is only about 30 m high.

quiz_bank.prompt: Chhattisgarh's state animal, the wild water buffalo, is common in its forests.
quiz_bank.explanation: Only a few dozen survive in central India, with very few females; six were brought from Assam to breed.

quiz_bank.prompt: What is the Laxman temple at Sirpur mainly built of?
quiz_bank.explanation: Brick, around 595 to 605 CE, with a stone door frame.

quiz_bank.prompt: What makes the Tala Rudra-Shiva unusual?
quiz_bank.explanation: Its features and body are formed from animals and extra faces.
options: Its body is made of animals and faces

quiz_bank.prompt: Why was Vir Narayan Singh first arrested in 1856?
quiz_bank.explanation: For giving a merchant's stored grain to famine victims.

quiz_bank.prompt: Gunda Dhur, leader of the 1910 Bhumkal, was captured and hanged.
quiz_bank.explanation: He was never caught.

quiz_bank.prompt: Gondi belongs to which language family?
quiz_bank.explanation: Dravidian, related to Telugu, not to Hindi.

quiz_bank.prompt: A ghotul is a Muria youth house where unmarried young people learn work, songs and rules.
quiz_bank.explanation: Verrier Elwin called it a children's republic.

quiz_bank.prompt: Why did the Ramnami founder tattoo Ram on his forehead?
quiz_bank.explanation: He had been refused entry to a temple because of caste.

quiz_bank.prompt: What is the jaitkham?
quiz_bank.explanation: A white pole with a white flag, symbol of the Satnami path of Guru Ghasidas.
options: A white pole with a white flag

quiz_bank.prompt: Pandavani tells stories from which epic?
quiz_bank.explanation: The Mahabharata, usually with Bhima as hero.

quiz_bank.prompt: Teejan Bai sang Pandavani in the seated Vedamati style.
quiz_bank.explanation: She sang standing, in the improvised Kapalik style.

quiz_bank.prompt: In Bastar dhokra, the fine lines on the surface come from
quiz_bank.explanation: Threads of beeswax wound over the clay core before casting.

quiz_bank.prompt: Kosa silk comes from mulberry-fed silkworms.
quiz_bank.explanation: It is tussar, from wild silkworms on forest trees.

quiz_bank.prompt: Why does chapda chutney taste sour?
quiz_bank.explanation: The ants contain formic acid.

quiz_bank.prompt: Bore Basi Tihar is held on
quiz_bank.explanation: 1 May, Labour Day, since 2022.

quiz_bank.prompt: At Bastar Dussehra, a giant Ravana effigy is burnt on the last day.
quiz_bank.explanation: No Ravana is burnt; the festival honours Danteshwari and village deities.

quiz_bank.prompt: At Hareli, children walk on
quiz_bank.explanation: Gedi, bamboo stilts, used until Pola.

quiz_bank.prompt: Chhattisgarh's share of rural population in 2011 (about 77%) was higher or lower than India's (about 69%)?
quiz_bank.explanation: Higher: 76.8% against 68.8%.

quiz_bank.prompt: Bhilai Steel Plant was built with help from
quiz_bank.explanation: The Soviet Union, from 1955.

quiz_bank.prompt: Chhattisgarh is the only Indian state that produces tin concentrate.
quiz_bank.explanation: According to the Indian Bureau of Mines.

quiz_bank.prompt: In 2011 the Supreme Court ruled against Salwa Judum's
quiz_bank.explanation: Use of armed civilians as special police officers.

quiz_bank.prompt: Which top Maoist leader was killed in Abujhmarh in May 2025?
quiz_bank.explanation: Basavaraju (Nambala Keshava Rao), the CPI (Maoist) general secretary.

quiz_bank.prompt: Where did the Union Home Minister declare India Naxal-free in May 2026?
quiz_bank.explanation: Jagdalpur, Bastar, on 20 May 2026.

side_dish.title: The resource curse, in plain words
side_dish.body_md:
Chhattisgarh sits on a fifth of India's coal output, rich iron ore and all its tin, yet for most of its life it has been one of the poorer states, and its richest mineral district, Bastar, was the poorest and most violent. Economists have a name for that pattern: the **resource curse**. Richard Auty coined it in 1993, and Jeffrey Sachs and Andrew Warner found that countries rich in natural resources had, on average, grown more slowly than resource-poor ones.

Why would wealth in the ground make people poorer? Three mechanisms are well studied.

**Dutch disease.** When a resource booms, money and workers flow to it and away from farming and manufacturing. When the boom ends, there is little else left. The name comes from the Netherlands after it found natural gas in 1959.

**Rent-seeking.** Minerals produce rents: profit that does not depend on effort. Whoever controls the licence collects them. Rulers who live on rents do not need taxes from citizens, so they need less of the citizens' consent.

**Conflict.** Valuable, stationary resources give armed groups something to fight over and to tax. Bastar's Maoists raised money by taxing contractors and traders.

The curse is not destiny. Norway and Botswana did well with oil and diamonds because institutions were strong before the money arrived. India's District Mineral Foundations, set up in 2015, try to send part of mining royalties back to the districts that are mined.

Try it today: when you read a news story about a mine, ask who gets the rent, who bears the dust, and who decides.

offline_task.title: Make chila and tomato chutney for breakfast
offline_task.body_md:
**Serves 2 (about 6 chila). 25 minutes. No soaking, no fermenting.**

**You need**
- 1 cup rice flour
- About 1 to 1¼ cups water
- ½ teaspoon salt, 1 green chilli finely chopped, 2 tablespoons chopped coriander, 1 small onion very finely chopped (optional)
- Oil for the pan
- For the chutney: 2 ripe tomatoes, 2 garlic cloves, 1 or 2 dry red chillies, salt, a few coriander leaves

**Steps**
1. Chutney first. Roast the tomatoes directly over a flame (or in a dry pan) until the skin blackens and splits. Toast the garlic and red chillies for a minute. Peel the tomatoes and crush everything with salt on a stone or in a mortar, keeping it coarse. Add coriander.
2. Whisk the rice flour, salt and water into a thin, lump-free batter, thinner than dosa batter, like pouring cream. Stir in chilli, coriander and onion. Rest 10 minutes.
3. Heat a heavy pan or tawa until a drop of water sizzles. Smear a few drops of oil.
4. Stir the batter (rice flour sinks), pour a ladle in the centre and quickly tilt the pan to spread it thin. It will look lacy.
5. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edge. Cover for a minute. Cook until the bottom is pale gold and the top is set. Flip briefly, or serve one side cooked.
6. Eat hot with the chutney.

**Notice** how different it is from a dosa: no lentils, no sourness, soft not crisp. That is the plain, rice-first taste of the Chhattisgarh plains.
